call_query_api.title: Call a query-protocol AWS service
call_query_api.description: Call a service that uses the AWS query protocol -- IAM, STS, SQS, EC2, SNS, RDS, CloudFormation, Auto Scaling and the rest. `action` and `version` name the operation (both come from that service's API reference), and `parameters` carries its arguments. Lists must be pre-flattened into AWS's numbered form, e.g. {"Filters.member.1.Name": "instance-state-name", "Filters.member.1.Value.1": "running"}. The connection signs for one AWS service (the integration's `service`, e.g. s3 or execute-api) in one region, so only that service's host answers.

request.description: The whole form body, including `Action` and `Version` -- e.g. {"Action": "DescribeInstances", "Version": "2016-11-15", "MaxResults": "10"}. Both `Action` and `Version` are required by the protocol, and `Version` differs per service.

output.description: The service's response. Query-protocol services answer XML by default, returned here as text unless the service supports JSON.

call_json_api.title: Call a JSON-protocol AWS service
call_json_api.description: Call a service that uses the AWS JSON protocol -- DynamoDB, Athena, Kinesis, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch Logs, Step Functions, ECS. The operation goes in the `X-Amz-Target` header as `<TargetPrefix>.<Operation>` and the arguments in the JSON body; the target prefix is per service (`DynamoDB_20120810`, `AmazonAthena`, `AWSSecretsManager`) and is documented in that service's API reference. The connection signs for one AWS service (the integration's `service`, e.g. s3 or execute-api) in one region, so only that service's host answers.

payload.description: The operation's arguments as JSON, exactly as that service's API reference documents them.

content_type.description: The JSON protocol version the service speaks -- "application/x-amz-json-1.0" (DynamoDB) or "-1.1" (most others).

get_rest_resource.title: Read from a REST-protocol AWS service
get_rest_resource.description: GET a path on a service that exposes a real REST API -- S3, API Gateway, ECR, EventBridge, Inspector, MediaConvert. You supply the path and query exactly as that service's reference documents them.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service, e.g. "/restapis" for API Gateway or "/2015-03-31/functions" for Lambda.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object.

output.description: Whatever the service returns, parsed as JSON where possible.

post_rest_resource.title: POST to a REST path
post_rest_resource.description: POST a JSON body to a path on the configured AWS service, SigV4-signed: invoke an API Gateway route, create a resource on a REST-protocol service, or start an operation. Use call_query_api or call_json_api for services that speak those protocols instead.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service, starting with /, e.g. "/my-bucket/reports/q3.json" for S3 or "/prod/orders" for an API Gateway stage.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object. They are part of what SigV4 signs.

body.description: The JSON request body, as the service's API reference documents it.

output.description: The service's response body, parsed when it is JSON and returned as text (often XML) otherwise.

put_rest_resource.title: PUT to a REST path
put_rest_resource.description: PUT a JSON body to a path on the configured AWS service, SigV4-signed: create or replace the resource at that path. For an S3 object whose content is not JSON, use put_object_content.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service, starting with /, e.g. "/my-bucket/reports/q3.json" for S3 or "/prod/orders" for an API Gateway stage.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object. They are part of what SigV4 signs.

body.description: The JSON request body, as the service's API reference documents it.

output.description: The service's response body, parsed when it is JSON and returned as text (often XML) otherwise.

patch_rest_resource.title: PATCH a REST path
patch_rest_resource.description: PATCH a path on the configured AWS service, SigV4-signed: a partial update on the services that support it, such as API Gateway's patchOperations.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service, starting with /, e.g. "/my-bucket/reports/q3.json" for S3 or "/prod/orders" for an API Gateway stage.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object. They are part of what SigV4 signs.

body.description: The JSON request body, as the service's API reference documents it.

output.description: The service's response body, parsed when it is JSON and returned as text (often XML) otherwise.

delete_rest_resource.title: DELETE a REST path
delete_rest_resource.description: DELETE a path on the configured AWS service, SigV4-signed. This removes real resources: an S3 object, an API Gateway deployment, a Lambda function. There is no undo beyond whatever versioning the service itself keeps.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service, starting with /, e.g. "/my-bucket/reports/q3.json" for S3 or "/prod/orders" for an API Gateway stage.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object. They are part of what SigV4 signs.

output.description: The service's response body, parsed when it is JSON and returned as text (often XML) otherwise.

put_object_content.title: PUT raw content
put_object_content.description: PUT a raw, already-encoded body to a path, SigV4-signed, with the content type you name. This is how to write an S3 object (text, CSV, XML, JSON as a string) or send an XML body to a REST-XML service such as S3 or Route 53.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service, starting with /, e.g. "/my-bucket/reports/q3.json" for S3 or "/prod/orders" for an API Gateway stage.

content.description: The body to send, exactly as it should arrive. Text only; binary content cannot be passed through this tool.

content_type.description: Media type of the content, e.g. text/plain, text/csv, application/xml.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object. They are part of what SigV4 signs.

output.description: The service's response body, parsed when it is JSON and returned as text (often XML) otherwise.

post_raw_content.title: POST raw content
post_raw_content.description: POST a raw, already-encoded body to a path, SigV4-signed, with the content type you name. Use it for REST-XML operations that take an XML document (S3 multi-object delete, Route 53 change batches, CloudFront invalidations) or any endpoint that does not take JSON.

path.description: The path to call on the configured service, starting with /, e.g. "/my-bucket/reports/q3.json" for S3 or "/prod/orders" for an API Gateway stage.

content.description: The body to send, exactly as it should arrive, e.g. an XML document.

query.description: Query-string parameters as a flat object. They are part of what SigV4 signs.

output.description: The service's response body, parsed when it is JSON and returned as text (often XML) otherwise.
